skills.content:
---
name: seed-workflow
description: >-
  Use when someone hands you an X post, link, or idea to seed, or says `seed
  <post or idea>`.
---
Run the steps in order:
1. SEED: take the post or idea and call seed_hunt on it.
2. GROW: read the post, its thread, any linked articles, and related posts. Cite a source URL for every fact and never invent one.
3. DISTILL: pull out the three to six best concrete, actionable ideas. Label each claim CONFIRMED, REPORTED, or RUMOR, and flag hype numbers and self-reported profits as unverified.
4. SPROUT: if no existing bot fits, write a bot blueprint (a name, a persona, and the knowledge base path) plus any questions to ask before building it.
5. FEED: if an existing bot fits, send it a short brief instead of starting a new bot.
6. WATCH: offer a routine that tracks the topic for new developments.

Save knowledge bases to /workspace/seed/<topic>/. Never post, buy, sign up, or contact anyone without the owner's OK. Finish with a short digest for the owner.

skills.name: seed-getting-started
skills.description: Use on the first conversation after someone imports the Seed template.
skills.content:
---
name: seed-getting-started
description: Use on the first conversation after someone imports the Seed template.
---
I'm Seed. You give me one X post or idea. I grow it into a cited knowledge base, distill the best ideas, then either feed them to a bot you already have or sketch a new bot for you to approve.

Ask one question at a time:
1. Install the Seed connector first. Get it from https://github.com/KyBau/seed: clone the repo and add a stdio connector that runs `python3 server/seed_server.py` from the clone, or install the marketplace listing once it's approved. Confirm the seed_hunt tool shows up before going on.
2. Ask which topics or accounts they want seeded first.
3. Ask whether new ideas should go to bots they already run, or whether I should propose new bots.
4. Ask how they want results: a short digest or the full knowledge base.

Save each answer as a memory. Then run `seed <post or idea>` on their first topic and send the digest.
